blocks.text:
Palay farming runs on a count. PhilRice ties its advice to days after transplanting (DAT) or after sowing (DAS). So a top dressing that is right on day 25 is a week late on day 32.

PhilRice's PalayCheck System sums up good rice management in nine Key Checks, from quality seed to dry, clean grain. Each season then ends with a loop: observe, measure and record, compare, and fix the weak spot next time. A good rice farming app is a tool for that loop. This guide covers rice only. For farms with other crops too, read our guide to the [best farm management app in the Philippines](/blog/farm-management-app-philippines).
Key points

items: Pick an app that counts DAS or DAT from each lot's own day zero.
Check it against the PalayCheck areas, from seed to postharvest.
It should also keep labor and harvest records, track typhoons, work offline and cost little.
anee.io does this from its free Libre plan up. The free PhilRice and DA tools answer other questions.

blocks.text: Why the count must belong to each lot

Few farmers plant every paddy on one day. PalayCheck's Key Check 3 asks you to plant within 14 days of the regular schedule of your irrigation service area. So two lots on one farm can sit ten days apart and both be on time.

That is why each lot needs its own count. In anee.io, every lot keeps its own day zero and its own growth stage. If a lot falls behind after a dry spell, Realign by Anee reads its records and moves its stage count to match, using credits.
How can a rice farming app help me run a small rice farm?
An app does not plant or spray for you. It remembers the plan, tells you what is due, and adds up what happened. Here is one palay season in anee.io.

items.title: Before day zero
items.text: Write the season in the [Protocol Builder](/features/protocol-builder), each fertilizer and spray on its DAS or DAT. See [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) for the field work.

items.title: On day zero
items.text: Add each paddy as a lot with its variety and size, then mark the sowing or transplanting day. The [cropping calendar](/features/cropping-calendar) dates every task.

items.title: From tillering to panicle initiation
items.text: Each top dressing shows on its day. Tick it done, and on Solo Farmer the shed takes the urea out of stock.

items.title: When something looks wrong
items.text: Pick palay in the free Pest Finder, or send Anee a photo and ask in Tagalog.

items.title: When a storm comes
items.text: Satellite Weather, which runs on credits, shows each typhoon's path and distance from your field. Then decide early if a spray should wait.

items.title: After harvest
items.text: Write each lot's yield, moisture, price and buyer in Observations, and the reports add up the season.

blocks.text: Fertilizer application for rice, on the right day

Fertilizer application for rice follows the stage, not the month. PalayCheck's Key Check 5 asks for enough nutrients from tillering to early panicle initiation and flowering. Our guide to [fertilizer for rice](/blog/fertilizer-for-rice) gives the PhilRice timings by DAT. Once those doses sit in your protocol, the app dates each one for every lot.

blocks.title: Put the Key Checks on the board
blocks.text: Add a short task for each check you can see. For example, count the hills per square meter after transplanting, and look at the grains before harvest. PalayCheck says to harvest by hand once 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. A check on the board gets ticked, while one in a booklet slips.

blocks.text: PhilRice reports that the Rice Crop Manager Advisory Service is free. In Tarlac, one farmer who followed it cut his fertilizer from 12 bags to 6, and his yield rose from 4 to 5.5 tons per hectare. That is one farmer's season, not a promise. Our guide to the [PalayCheck key checks](/blog/palaycheck-key-checks) explains each check.
Where does anee.io fall short for rice?

items: Anee needs internet and uses credits. The board and notes work offline, but her answers wait for a signal.
It does not run PalayCheck assessments or count panicles. You write the checks into your plan.
Libre holds one active season with one lot, and shows a few ads.
Its screens are in English. Anee is the part that answers in Tagalog, Bisaya or Ilocano.

blocks.text: Questions about rice farming apps

items.q: What is the best rice farming app in the Philippines?
items.a: Look for one that counts DAS or DAT for each lot, follows the palay growth stages and keeps labor and harvest records. It must also work offline. anee.io does all of this and starts free.

items.q: Is there a free rice farming app?
items.a: Yes. PhilRice's PalayCheck App and Binhing Palay show a price of zero on Google Play, and the Rice Crop Manager Advisory Service is free on the web. Libre, the anee.io free plan, works too, with a few ads.

items.q: Can a rice farming app tell me when to apply fertilizer?
items.a: It puts each dose on its day once the plan is set. In anee.io, you write the fertilizer tasks on their DAS or DAT, or ask Anee for a Crop Protocol Analysis. Still, take the rates from a soil test, MOET or the Rice Crop Manager.

items.q: Will a rice farming app raise my yield?
items.a: No app can promise a harvest. It helps you do the right work on the right day and keep honest records. Your yield still depends on seed, soil, water, weather and care.
